cpuThrottle.scope: openProbe and after-open counters precede CPU throttling; subsequent netplay setup and first game callback use the configured per-side rates.

headedLaunch.scope: Window-mode environment control, not a production code change; proxy, input, audio/context, CPU setup, and native GPU arguments are unchanged.

injection.packetScope: E9NP version 4 kind 1; ACK-only and redundant input included; non-input control/hash/signaling untouched; relay has no separate RTC repair lane.
injection.jitterAlgorithm: Per-sender LCG 1664525*x+1013904223, seed 0x915ab+sender; same formula as legacy client impairment. Relay forwarding order can differ.
injection.burstClock: First non-empty E9NP input receive in this relay process; distinct from browser active time.

hostObservation.scope: Original host samples remain in the raw source; no samples excluded by host load.

method.window: Each peer largest formal actual request-to-entry wait; [request,entry), plus the intersection of the two windows. Browser RAF timestamps are retained but not substituted for actual entry.
method.clock: Browser performance.timeOrigin comes from both setup and final headed observations, checked equal per page; offset=pageOrigin-relay.clock.started.timeOrigin. Cross-process clock error was not calibrated.
method.joins: Use explicit receiveEventId and scheduledId. Verify receive-to-schedule header/FNV fields excluding destination, and schedule-to-send full header/FNV/destination. Preserve each event occurrence; no deduplication.
method.scope: Relay JavaScript receive callback, injection scheduling and original WebSocket.send call only. These are not OS arrival, browser delivery, or native acceptance timestamps.
method.quantiles: Sorted array at floor(count*p), matching current harness summary convention.
method.lcg: Recomputed all scheduled delays in source event order independently per sender: uint32(1664525*seed+1013904223), initial seed=0x915ab+sender; delay=39+(seed/2^32*2-1)*5.

findings: The independent relay continued receiving, scheduling, forwarding and firing its 100 ms timing probe throughout both approximately 1.4 s browser RAF pending windows.
In the shared window there are 71 receives, 71 schedules, 77 sends and 13 timing ticks. The largest recorded relay heartbeat gap in that window is 114.2729 ms.
All 5602 planned delays exactly match the declared 39 +/- 5 ms LCG condition within 1e-10 ms; planned values span 34.006384..43.998611 ms. The condition was exercised, not merely requested.
Whole-trace schedule-to-send max is 76.4138 ms; schedules inside the shared RAF gap reach at most 55.1099 ms and 54.9884 ms by sender. No measured relay scheduling segment explains a 1.4 s hold.

Every observed receive has a schedule and every observed send has a matching schedule with unchanged header/FNV fields. Three final ACK-only scheduled jobs have no terminal event at snapshot and remain pending.

Source FrameSchedule retries blocked input on subsequent RAF callbacks; it does not gate dispatch of an already requested browser RAF on network readiness. Network shortage may explain lack of logical progress in dispatched callbacks, but this relay trace does not explain absence of dispatch.
limitations: NETWORK_TRACE=0: browser WS send/message and positive native poll-copy timestamps are not available. Do not assign a receiver-side delivery delay, native acceptance time or end-to-end packet latency.
Continuous relay receipt does not prove continuous browser native pumping; upstream buffering and browser scheduling were not individually observed in this trace.
Selected relay packet headers in the gap retain the same latest-input frontiers; they are redundant traffic, not evidence that fresh logical inputs continued to be produced.
Send-minus-due residuals include negative values and are retained in statistics and window records. Timer scheduling is not a hard real-time deadline; no residual was clamped or filtered.
The ending-window pending ACK-only jobs remain incomplete, including one already 4.393 ms past its due time when snapshotting stopped. Their later completion is not claimed.
Timing-window joins use timeOrigin across processes without an independent calibration; bounds close to an event should not be treated as sub-millisecond causal proof.
Host measurements are retained in the original source; no host-load filter or attribution to a compiler, OS, GPU, browser internals or security service is made.
The source report passed integrity gates, but the simultaneous large new-state gaps remain adverse user-experience evidence. No new run, build or harness change was made for this analysis.
